question: Which of the following led to reservation of industrial activities for private and public sectors for the first time in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 marked a significant step in India's economic planning by reserving certain industries exclusively for the public and private sectors.
 
• This policy aimed to accelerate industrialization and create a mixed economy where both public and private sectors would play pivotal roles.
 
• Under this resolution, industries were classified into three categories: Schedule A, Schedule B, and Schedule C.
 
• Schedule A included industries that would be exclusively owned by the State, Schedule B included industries where the State would play a dominant role, and Schedule C consisted of the remaining industries left to the private sector.
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 laid the foundation for the development of the heavy industries and infrastructure sectors in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948**

 
 
• This was the first major industrial policy statement by the Government of India after independence, which aimed to outline the role of the state in industrial development.
 
• It categorized industries into four broad areas based on state involvement and control.
 
 
 
• **Industries Development and Regulation Act, 1951**
 
 
• This Act provided the framework for the central government to regulate and control the establishment and functioning of industries in India.
 
• It aimed to ensure planned and coordinated development of industries across the country.
 
 
 
• **Statement of Industrial Policy, 1945**
 
 
• This pre-independence policy aimed to promote industrialization by providing incentives and removing barriers to industrial growth.
 
• It focused on reconstruction and development post-World War II.
